Title: LSJ: Petra Resonance and empty crypt

Messages.Author: Blooded Sand
Messages.Body:
This came up last night.

John plays Petra resonance, with only John and Mike left in the game.
Mike has no crypt left.
What happens?

I said the card fizzles as there is no vampires to reveal, so nothing
happens, but am unsure if it should not have been everyone burns one
pool, as there is a tie for the lowest and highest revealed vamp (the
only revealed vamp ties itself).

Petra Resonance
Type: Action
Requires: Malkavian
+1 stealth action. Not usable if any Methuselah's crypt is empty.
Each Methuselah reveals the top card of his or her crypt. If there is
a tie for highest or lowest cost among the revealed cards, every
Methuselah burns 1 pool. Otherwise, the Methuselah revealing the
highest cost steals 3 pool from the Methuselah revealing the lowest
cost. All Methuselahs shuffle their crypts afterward.

Messages.Author: floppyzedolfin
Messages.Body:


I'm not sure it would completely fizzle.
With similar cardtext ("Only usable if [...]"), there's this ruling
about Edge Vitiation and loosing the Edge:
http://groups.google.com/group/rec.games.trading-cards.jyhad/msg/2a438c49077bc5fa

Similarly, if a vampire untaps from Rutor's Hand, Temptation, or Earth
Meld + Obedience, I don't think his Force of Will bleed would fizzle.

I suppose that, if Petra Resonance follows the other rulings, at
successful resolution, all Methuselahs without an empty crypt would
reveal their top crypt card.
If there is a tie for highest or lowest or a highest and a lowest
(each of these requires two vampires at least revealed), then magic
happens for those revealing. Those not revealing are unaffected.

If only 1 vampire is revealed, there is no tie. I'm not sure it would
be meaningful to have the player steal 3 pool from herself, but if
that was how things happen, then even if the only Methuselah revealing
a vampire were on 1-2-3 pool, she'd survive this (as the gaining and
loosing is simultaneous) and there would be no alteration to the game
state.

If no crypt card is revealed (it could happen, in some extremely weird
cases), then... nothing happens.

Messages.Author: LSJ
Messages.Body:

> tie

> 4 [no object] achieve the same score or ranking as another competitor
>

> I'd say it's not a tie if there's only 1 person in the challenge.

Correct.

The card doesn't ask if the highest = the lowest. It asks if there is
a tie for highest (or a tie for lowest).
In this case, there is not. There is a single highest (no tie). And a
single lowest (no tie).

To claim that the series <8> has a tie is to claim that the series
<4,5,8> has a tie -- there are just as many "highest" capacities in
<4,5,8> as there are in <8>.

For instance, if I play solitare (bowling, say) and achieve a score of
47 (I'm really good at bowling :-), I win (since no one scored
higher). I am not tied for the win.
